frozen.change: Object model v1 frozen for team use and 7-SaaS measurement through PR #117 (AEGI-Inc/aegi-dashboard). Later model work happens as v2 on a separate track; v1 artifacts change only by an explicit new decision.

profiles.evidence: GH-23 enterprise is the parent organization boundary. Interface Tenant criterion; resolves the draft model abstention for this collected record.
GH-01 organization is the tenant scope for repositories, users and installations. Its enterprise parent is retained when returned; otherwise it is the observed collection boundary.
GH-02 user id is a permission-bearing account. User type distinguishes Bot from User.
GH-05 persistent repository id is an explicit permission target.
Q1: organization team; membership and repository role grants refer to this team.
GH-07 independently managed repository permission bundle.
GH-14 tenant-scoped installation, distinct from the global App artifact and grants.
GH-13 independently revocable organization authorization for a PAT. This record is a grant, not the secret material of the token; expiry is read from token_expires_at when present.
GH-22 independently revocable SAML credential authorization; missing expiry stays unknown.
GH-08 independently managed repository rules and conditions.
GH-09 branch-scoped independently managed protection rule.
GH-10 executable workflow definition; runs are kept in the observation plane.
GH-15 callback address crossing the tenant boundary. Hosting ownership is not inferred from arbitrary hostnames.
Persistent Git object addressed by SHA, tree and parents; not an execution instance.
GH-12 persistent editable review object inside its repository.

v2 decision V2-P1 (A05). GH-24 deployment environment inside a repository, holding its own secrets and protection rules. Required reviewers stay references; the environment is not itself a permission target here.

v2 decision V2-P1 (A01). GH-25 repository or environment Actions secret. The API returns only name and dates; the value is stored in the tenant and handed to workflows, so material is tenant_side and rotation is api. What the value is (token, key) is not returned: credential_kind stays unresolved. No expiry is returned: unknown, not unbounded.

v2 decision V2-P1 (A01). GH-25 organization Actions secret; visibility all, private or selected. Selected repositories are an available_to reference, not a relation: no closed relation type means "usable by". Value kind and expiry are not returned.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A01). GH-25 repository Dependabot secret; same contract as the Actions secret.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A01). GH-25 organization Dependabot secret; same contract as the organization Actions secret.

v2 decision V2-P1 (A02). GH-26 SSH deploy key of one repository. The private key stays with whoever deploys; GitHub holds the public key (kept as a fingerprint). read_only selects the read or write role of has_role_on: the permits template has no role slot, has_role_on admits a Credential source. No expiry is returned.

v2 decision V2-P1 (A03). GH-27 organization role (predefined or custom) with its permission list. Team and user assignments are has_role_on the organization with this role in the role slot; user rows inherited through a team are computed.

v2 decision V2-P1 (A04). GH-28 IdP group visible to an Enterprise Managed Users organization. A connected team takes its members from the group: group member_of team. The identity Link to the IdP group (Okta) needs a crosswalk rule and is left open.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B01). GH-29 pending organization invitation with its role; independently cancellable. Until accepted it grants nothing, so no access relation is made: invitee and inviter stay references.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B03). GH-30 branch or tag name pattern that may deploy to one environment; applies_to that environment.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B03). GH-30 custom deployment protection rule run by a GitHub App; applies_to its environment. The App is a reference, not a relation.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B05). GH-31 organization IP allow list entry. It sits in the organization (tenant reference) without a relation, as the judgment table recommended.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B06). GH-31 organization SAML identity provider: registered_in the organization. The IdP signing certificate is not collected.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B08). GH-31 verified or approved organization domain that limits notification email routing. The verification token is not collected.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B07). GH-32 organization runner group holding self-hosted runners. Research interface Resource is kept. Selected repositories that may use it are an available_to reference, as for organization secrets.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B07). GH-32 self-hosted runner machine registration, contained_in its runner group. Registration tokens are not collected.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B09). GH-33 organization package; contained_in its linked repository when one is named.
OK-01 organization is the root identity and policy boundary.
OK-02 permission-bearing account. Management User has no reliable human/service flag: unknown is retained.
OK-03 group can be assigned roles and application access.

OK-04 enrolled authentication factor. Pinned Okta Profile declares device-side material and no factor expiry. factorType selects an explicit credential-kind subtype; unsupported types remain unresolved.
OK-05 independently managed IAM role definition.
OK-05 resource selector set is an editable target collection, distinct from IamRole permission definitions.
OK-07/09 tenant application registration. URL, permissions and material must be routed away from the Integration.
OK-07 application-user binding; composite app/user identity, independently removable while both endpoints remain. scope USER/GROUP is scalar provenance, not a scope list.
OK-07 independently removable application-group binding; composite app/group identity.

OK-08 OAuth client application registered in the tenant. User decision GC (2026-10-19): no stored secret, so not Credential; the client itself is an Integration, not a separate Principal. Administrative grants stay has_role_on from this Integration. Same-entity review with the Okta Application remains open.
OK-09 actual refresh-token record identified by token id. Missing expiresAt is unknown, not unbounded.
OK-11 independently managed condition/action rule that assigns other group memberships: both Policy and executable Automation definition.
OK-10 independently managed security policy definition.
OK-10 rule definition under policy; discriminator variants share policy-rule identity and retain include/exclude fields.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A06). OK-15 API service integration instance registered in the tenant.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A06). OK-15 API service integration secret. Plaintext secret value is never returned; hash or fingerprint is retained.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A07). OK-16 API token issued to a user for administrative/management API calls. The token plaintext is never returned after creation; token metadata and expiry are retained.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A08). OK-17 outbound event hook endpoint delivering events outside the tenant boundary.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A08). OK-17 synchronous bidirectional inline hook endpoint invoked during authentication or user registration flows.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A08). OK-17 outbound log streaming endpoint.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A09). OK-18 external identity provider (IdP) integration configured in the tenant.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B10). OK-19 attribute expressions that copy profile values between an application user profile and the Okta user profile on every sync. owned_by the application side when it is collected, otherwise the org.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B11). OK-20 X.509 signing certificate of an external IdP, kept only as a fingerprint. The signing private key stays with the IdP. owned_by the org; an IdP whose protocol trust names this kid authenticates_with it. expiresAt is a row field.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B12). OK-21 inbound Shared Signals receiver configuration: an outside transmitter posts security events into the tenant, receives_into the org. The research type also lists Integration; the judgment table chose the Endpoint profile.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B12). OK-21 Shared Signals transmitter stream delivering Okta security events to a receiver outside the tenant; owned_by the org.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B13). OK-21 custom SMTP server through which Okta sends its mail; owned_by the org. The SMTP password is not kept.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B15). OK-22 org authenticator configuration (which factor kinds are enabled). Policy rules keep their own field references; no relation is drawn to them.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B15). OK-22 origin allowed for CORS, redirect or iFrame embedding; a tenant rule without relations.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B15). OK-22 device assurance policy (OS version, encryption, screen lock). Policy rules reference it by id; no relation is drawn.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B15). OK-22 network zone (IP, ASN, location lists). Policy rule network conditions reference it by id; no relation is drawn.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B17). OK-23 pool of on-premises agents (AD, LDAP, RADIUS) that connect directories to the tenant; registered_in the org. Research interface Integration is kept.
SL-00 explicitly returned enterprise_id is the root organization boundary; workspace is a nested tenant.
SL-00 team.info identifies the workspace under the returned enterprise, or the workspace boundary when no enterprise parent is returned.
SL-01/02 user id is a permission-bearing identity; bot/user distinction is retained from source flags.
SL-07 bot identity is separate from the associated U-prefixed bot user.
SL-10 manifest bot scopes are requested permissions, not evidence that a token was issued. Upgrade to Credential only when D-21 OAuth response contains a stored material fingerprint.
SL-03 persistent conversation; explicit membership and posting target.
SL-06/15 user group; same usergroups.list record called subteam in the legacy schema.
SL-05 persistent message addressed by channel plus timestamp; differs from admin analytics message aggregates and audit events.
SL-07/08 and D-21 tenant-scoped bot/OAuth installation facts. An external global app listing alone cannot create this registration.
SL-10 manifest features.slash_commands[].url is an outbound request and response endpoint; retain actual routing, do not infer hosting ownership from a domain.
D-21 OAuth response explicitly returns a bearer webhook and channel. Keep only URL fingerprint and source redaction path; install x credential kind identity.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B19). SL-17 Workflow Builder workflow. owned_by the app that made it when collected, otherwise the enterprise. Steps and functions are properties as the judgment table recommended; step inputs keep names only because values carry message text. Who it runs as is not returned.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B19). SL-17 collaborator binding of a user to one workflow, independently removable (admin.workflows.collaborators.remove). The binding is kept as an Assignment record and the user has_role_on the workflow with role collaborator. The research has no record type for the bare ID list.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B20). SL-18 information barrier: the primary user group may not reach the barriered groups over the restricted subjects. applies_to the primary user group; barriered groups are references.
GW-01 customer is the root Workspace identity boundary.
GW-03 Directory user identity holds Workspace roles; email alone does not classify human versus service.
Q3/GW-04 Directory and Cloud Identity Group refer to the same customer group.
GW-04 independently removable Directory group membership. This is not Meet Member and not a new User entity.
GW-06 role definition contains an explicit privilege bundle.
GW-06 independently removable role assignment; expirationDetails must be preserved when returned. Absence is not silently converted to never-expiring.
GW-05 tokens.list returns user/client authorization metadata and scopes, not access-token material. User x client identifies revocable consent; client remains an external locator.

v2 decision V2-R1. GW-15 users.settings.delegates.list: a delegate can read and send mail for the mailbox owner. The record is revocable on its own (delete the delegate) while both users remain, so it is an Assignment; Gmail gives it no expiry. The mailbox is not a separate Object, so no has_role_on is drawn; the delegate user is the grantee reference and an outside address stays an external locator.
GW-07 persistent Drive file, folder scope and explicit grant target.
GW-07 independently removable file permission; expirationTime is a row field and must not be guessed.
GW-08 persistent editable form; linked sheet stays a reference without inventing a relation vocabulary entry.
GW-09 persistent Apps Script project and executable source definition. Process records remain observations; execution identity is row evidence, otherwise unknown.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A10). GW-17 Cloud Identity Inbound SAML SSO Profile represents external SAML IdP configuration for inbound federation.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A10). GW-17 Cloud Identity Inbound OIDC SSO Profile represents external OIDC IdP configuration for inbound federation.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A10). GW-17 Cloud Identity IdP Credential (X.509 certificate) for Inbound SAML SSO Profile. Certificate material is fingerprinted (sha256).
v2 decision V2-P1 (A10). GW-17 Cloud Identity Inbound SSO Assignment links an SSO profile to target groups or organizational units.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A11). GW-18 user app-specific password. Plaintext password is never returned; metadata and user association are retained.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A12). GW-19 shared drive (Team Drive) is a top-level container for shared file permissions and explicit grant target.
v2 decision V2-P1 (A13). GW-20 Directory OrgUnit is a container for users; users connect via member_of. Interface Spec notes OrgUnit is not a grant target.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B21). GW-22 sharing rule of a user primary calendar (role and scope: user, group, domain or default). The calendar is a property of the rule, not an object, so no access relation is drawn; grantee and calendar owner stay references. The owner rule of the calendar owner itself is not kept.

v2 decision V2-P2 (B24, interface decided Policy). GW-23 external domain allowed for sharing and collaboration. A list of allowed domains is a rule, not an address, so Policy is kept instead of the research Endpoint.
v2 decision V2-P2 (B25). GW-24 Cloud Identity policy: one setting with its query. applies_to the single org unit or group the query names; a query without a single target stays a property.
SF-01 organization is the root boundary; every other record carries its org.
SF-02 user id is a permission-bearing account. UserType AutomatedProcess is a service identity; otherwise unknown is retained.
SF-03 profile is the base permission bundle of a user (ProfileId). Decision B6: has_role_on with the profile in the role slot.
SF-04 independently managed permission bundle. Profile-owned permission sets are the profile container and are not projected separately.
SF-04 independently revocable assignment of a permission set to a user. ExpirationDate null is vendor-declared no expiry; a date without a time zone is kept as a date, not converted.
SF-05 role hierarchy node. Decision B6: user role is has_role_on; decision B7: hierarchy is contained_in via ParentRoleId, inheritance is an Effective Access rule.
SF-06 public group or queue that receives sharing and record access.
SF-06 independently removable group membership row; the vendor has no membership expiry.
SF-07 connected app registered in the org. Cartography AUTHORIZED decision: user authorization is has_role_on to this app.

SF-07 user OAuth approval of a connected app. The record holds no token value, so the Credential criterion fails (same as Google Token). It links to the app only by name; the relation is computed and kept only for a unique name.
AT-01 Atlassian site is the tenant shared by Jira and Confluence. Research tagged ServerInformation as Integration; Cartography decision (Jira global admin targets the tenant) needs a Tenant.
JI-02 Atlassian account id is shared by Jira and Confluence permissions. accountType app is a service identity; otherwise unknown.
JI-03 site group by groupId; Q2 decision: the four Jira group views are one entity.
JI-04 project is the permission target of permission schemes and project roles. Project lead stays a property (Cartography LEADS decision).
JI-05 project role. Decisions B4, B5: actors are has_role_on with this role, target the project.
JI-06 permission scheme shared by projects.
JI-06 decision A17: independently removable scheme line. Decision B3: holder --[permission]--> each project using the scheme. Dynamic holders stay properties for Effective Access.
JI-07 saved filter; the owner can edit and share it (owned_by Resource -> Principal).
JI-07 decision A18: removable filter share. User and group shares are has_role_on view or edit; global shares are shared_with the site.
CF-01 Confluence space is the permission target of space permissions.
CF-02 removable space permission row: principal --[operation:target]--> space.
A role name explicitly present in a collected has_role_on relation is a scoped vendor permission-bundle key. Preserve only the declared name; do not infer capabilities.
A literal URL property on an Integration is projected to its own Endpoint with exact-address identity and owned_by registration; no hosting ownership is guessed.

link_only.evidence: User decision GF1 (2026-10-19): a SAML/SCIM external identity joins the same person across providers. It is identity Link evidence (M2 saml_external_identity), not an Assignment or Principal Object.

has_role_on.template: Principal | Policy | Credential | Integration --[Policy]--> Resource | Tenant | Integration | Automation

owned_by.template: Endpoint | Automation | Credential --> Integration | Tenant ; Resource --> Principal ; Principal --> Integration
